items.sentence: Ada Ríos *grew up* in a slum near the Cateura landfill in Paraguay.
Every morning, garbage trucks *rolled* into the landfill and *unloaded* tons of trash.
People in the slum then *looked* through the trash for things they could recycle or sell.
items.pattern: S + Vi + Prepositional phrase + Elliptical Relative clause

items.sentence: This *was* how they made a living, and Ada *believed* her future would be no different.
One day, Ada’s grandma *saw* a poster that said “Free music lessons from Mr. Chávez.”
Ada’s grandma *knew* Ada loved music, so she *applied* for Ada.
Ada really *looked forward to* the lessons.
She *wanted* to learn how to play the violin and be carried away by the power of music.
Ada and some other children *took* Mr. Chávez’s lessons, but there *were* not enough instruments.
Buying new ones *was* impossible, since a violin cost more than a local house!
items.pattern: Gerund Phrase (S) + Vi + C + Adverbial clause (since...)

items.sentence: Fortunately, a garbage picker who was good at using tools *learned* about their trouble and *tried* to use what was at hand.
items.pattern: S + Relative clause (who...) + Vt (Compound verb) + Noun clause

items.sentence: By putting together metal cans, forks, and other items from the landfill, the garbage picker somehow *managed* to make various instruments.
items.pattern: Prepositional phrase + S + Vt + Infinitival O

items.sentence: They *weren’t* very traditional and barely *cost* anything, but to these children they *were* invaluable.
At first, each child *played* in his or her own way, and only screeches *came* out of the instruments.
Some kids *quit* the music lessons after a few weeks, but with Mr. Chávez’s encouragement, Ada and the others *kept* practicing, sometimes for several hours a day.
Slowly, their musical skills *improved*.
They *began* to hit all the right notes and *played* together harmoniously.
Finally, they *formed* the “Recycled Orchestra.”
After the orchestra performed several local concerts, they *attracted* wider attention and even *received* invitations to perform abroad.
items.pattern: Adverbial clause (After...) + S + Vt (Compound verb) + O

items.sentence: Ada and the other members *visited* different countries.
The world *dazzled* them just as they dazzled the world.
items.pattern: S + Vt + O + Adverbial clause (just as...)

items.sentence: Four years later, a world-famous rock band *saw* the children’s potential and *invited* the orchestra to tour with them.
At their first concert with the band, Ada and her friends nervously *stepped* on stage in front of nearly 35,000 people.
items.pattern: Prepositional phrase + S + Vi + Prepositional phrase

items.sentence: They *saw* glaring lights and *heard* screams of excitement.
These children *felt* dizzy and *didn’t know* what to do.
However, as soon as the orchestra began to play, everyone *cheered*.
items.pattern: Adverbial clause (as soon as...) + S + Vi

items.sentence: When Ada and her friends bowed to the crowd at the end, they *knew* that the performance was a triumph.
items.pattern: Adverbial clause (When...) + S + Vt + Noun clause (that...)

items.sentence: Touring overseas *changed* their lives in other ways, too.
With the money they earned, Ada and her friends *had* larger, safer houses *built* for their families.
items.pattern: Prepositional phrase (with Elliptical Relative clause) + S + Vt + O + OC (p.p.)

items.sentence: More importantly, they *showed* the locals that children’s dreams didn’t have to end up in the trash.
Through determination and hard work, these children *were able to create* beauty out of garbage and *have* faith in their abilities to pursue greater things.
items.pattern: Prepositional phrase + S + Vt (Compound verb) + O

text_genre.raw_text: The text of “From Trash to Triumph” is a narrative text telling the story about how Ada and her friends changed their lives through their determination and hard work, rising from trash to triumph on stage. It follows the structure of a “story mountain” with the exposition (beginning), the rising action (build-up), the climax, the falling action, and the resolution (ending). Study the graphic organizer on page 158 and learn how to build a story mountain.
